author: Xovizo
quote:
Where to begin...

I cannot commit automobile theft in a game called Grand Theft Auto. This sentence essentially says it all. Rockstar Games, in the attempt to make hyper-realistic game, they ended up making it unbearable. We play games to dive into a virtual world and live a life that is completely fictional. In that life, anything is possible. When it comes to GTA 6, all of those couldn't be further away from being the case. In the pursuit of seriousness and realism, The studio has completely forgotten what constituted a great game. A great game is something you would like to come back to, to have fun. It's something that you turn your console ON for if you have a spare hour or two and it's something that if you have company, you could all have fun. GTA 6 is neither of those. In order to steal cars, you need to spend hours upon hours building mechanics to do so. In order to get the good ending you have to play a particular way that the developers have envisioned... It's not a game. It's a virtual life simulator. 

GTA has always been known for being the game where you can do it all. Being the game that does not judge you and allows you to be the craziest the most reckless player that you know would never exist in the real world. This is exactly the reason why we played those games. It's to do stuff that we cannot do in the real life. Some because they are illegal, others because they are unethical. But what does it matter? It's a darn video game about criminals as main characters. 

I don't want to start a game where I know that I have to plan my getaway. I do not want to start a game, where I have to change clothing, change vehicle or any other little aspect of the character in order for me to get away from being chased. I do not want to start a game where i have to do groceries, repair cars and houses in order to use them. I want to start a game where I am free to do anything. Whether it's to carry 60 weapons or break into a hypercar parked on the street. 
By trying to make this game overly realistic, Rockstar Games effectively brought the most boring aspects of real life into a con-led story game.

Additionally, following the online posts about the game displaying invincibility on particular NPCs, the developers are effectively telling us that we have to live by their morals. The removal of S*x workers, the inability to draw guns in particular areas or to drive through specific groups of people is a choice that should be left to the player. If the developers are very strict and sensitive about those aspects, don't bring them into the game. Morals should always be left to the player to decide. 

Lastly, I would like to cover the technical aspect of the game. 30 frames a second is not a problem at all as many people criticize... Your eyes get used to it within the first 15 minutes, and the game is gigantic and beautiful, which is why we are unable to run it on better specs. This part is totally understandable and completely fine and acceptable. What is unacceptable is to take away features that were available in previous games, and make them unavailable or un-functional in the current game. In particular I'm talking about air and sea travel having completely zero physics. Boats sailing at full speed have absolutely no impact onto objects they hit. Plane physics break entirely if you hit something from a front or if you leave the vehicle behind. But the saddest part is that the explosions and effects of destruction makes the game look like Fortnite instead of Grand Theft Auto. Their goal was to make the most realistic GTA up to this point but they decided to remove the far more realistic effects from the previous game for a spark explosion effect in this one? How is this possible? How come the wings on planes do not break when you hit a physical object? That's a feature that was present in a game that came out in 2013. 
Speaking of games that came out 13 years ago, what is going on with the plot? People responsible for script writing were trying to replicate a movie instead of creating a Satire video game. The characters are boring, the plot is uninteresting, and overall, this feels like one of the binge Netflix series instead of being a standalone story.

Oh and let's bring up the question of realism in which we have superhuman Hulk-esque characters, giant crabs, and "non-failable" mission sequences. It does not matter how bad you are, dying from the likes of an enemy is a crime. 

To conclude, this game broke the lineage of traditional Rockstar Grand Theft Auto games. Instead of making the games more fun with more options as well as more things that you can do, with an interesting story and unforgettable views (only present thing), we got ourselves a low-budget Netflix studio Drama movie. 

The expectations were high, but they were not unachievable for a company that had the budget to build a second Burj Khalifa. 

Hopefully this game serves Rockstar as a lesson for what NOT to do next.
